short: A North African general who won a four-way civil war and openly told his sons to keep the soldiers paid.
full:
Septimius Severus was proclaimed emperor by the Danube legions on 9 April 193 CE and spent his first four years defeating rival claimants before securing Rome and the frontiers alike. Born in Leptis Magna in modern Libya, he was the first emperor from Africa, and he governed as a soldier rather than a senator's favourite, raising military pay substantially and packing the Senate with loyalists from the provinces.

His reign set the tone for the century that followed: reported deathbed advice to his sons Caracalla and Geta was to enrich the soldiers and ignore everyone else. He died at York on 4 February 211 CE while campaigning in Britain, leaving the throne jointly to his two sons — an arrangement that collapsed within the year.
